title: Nuclear factor I-C as a novel candidate regulator in postoperative atrial fibrillation: integrated omics and proof-of-concept validation.
authors: Gao, Chaoyue; Shu, Yue; Luo, Lin; Wang, Ningning; Wang, Taiwei; Ren, Zexinyao; Shen, Pan; Liu, Yisi
one_liner_zh: 该文通过多组学整合和机器学习识别转录因子NFIC在术后房颤中的调控作用，但未涉及蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，仅用数据库预测靶基因，与课题核心关联较弱。
abstract: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is a frequent complication of cardiac surgery, yet the upstream transcriptional regulators driving the pro-arrhythmic substrate remain unexplored. We aimed to identify and validate key transcription factors associated with POAF susceptibility. We performed cross-cohort integration of two independent human atrial transcriptomic datasets and applied machine learning (LASSO and SVM-RFE) to prioritize candidate genes. Transcriptional targets were predicted using the TRRUST database and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis. Cellular localization was resolved using murine atrial scRNA-seq data. In vivo functional validation and biochemical signaling assays were performed in a spontaneous POAF (sPOAF) mouse model using AAV9-mediated NFIC overexpression. Nuclear Factor I-C (NFIC) was identified as a robust candidate regulator, showing consistent downregulation in human POAF cohorts and sPOAF mice. By intersecting predicted NFIC targets with the PI3K/Akt pathway, hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) was nominated as a putative downstream effector. Single-cell profiling localized NFIC and HGF predominantly to the atrial fibroblast lineage, where both were significantly downregulated in POAF. In the sPOAF model, p-AKT/AKT ratios were significantly reduced during the acute postoperative phase. Critically, AAV9-mediated NFIC restoration significantly decreased POAF incidence by 50%. Our findings identify NFIC as a novel candidate transcriptional regulator associated with POAF. These data support a working model involving a fibroblast-centered NFIC-HGF-PI3K/AKT axis, providing a fresh framework for understanding the upstream control of the postoperative atrial microenvironment.
abstract_zh: 术后心房颤动（POAF）是心脏手术的常见并发症，然而驱动促心律失常底物的上游转录调控因子尚未被探索。我们旨在识别并验证与POAF易感性相关的关键转录因子。我们对两个独立的人类心房转录组数据集进行了跨队列整合，并应用机器学习（LASSO和SVM-RFE）来优先排序候选基因。使用TRRUST数据库和蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络分析预测转录靶点。利用小鼠心房单细胞RNA测序（scRNA-seq）数据解析细胞定位。在自发性POAF（sPOAF）小鼠模型中，通过AAV9介导的NFIC过表达进行了体内功能验证和生化信号传导分析。核因子I-C（NFIC）被识别为稳健的候选调控因子，在人类POAF队列和sPOAF小鼠中均显示出一致的下调。通过将预测的NFIC靶点与PI3K/Akt通路相交集，肝细胞生长因子（HGF）被提名为推定的下游效应因子。单细胞分析将NFIC和HGF主要定位于心房成纤维细胞谱系，在POAF中两者均显著下调。在sPOAF模型中，急性术后阶段p-AKT/AKT比值显著降低。关键的是，AAV9介导的NFIC恢复使POAF发生率显著降低50%。我们的发现将NFIC识别为与POAF相关的新型候选转录调控因子。这些数据支持一个涉及成纤维细胞中心的NFIC-HGF-PI3K/AKT轴的working model，为理解术后心房微环境的上游调控提供了新框架。
